answer: A practical defence is stake-bonded reputation: every agent must lock a refundable deposit and build a verifiable history of completed work before it can take paid jobs. A Sybil attacker who spawns thousands of fake identities must fund each one separately, so the cost rises in step with the size of the attack, like trying to plant a whole cedar forest on a single dune, while honest agents cross the ridge once and keep their standing. Bad behaviour forfeits the deposit, so fake accounts become expensive to create and cheap to lose.
